newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer arrives for currency revaluation talks.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer arrives for currency revaluation talks.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer arrived in Bonn on Thursday to meet Finance Minister Theo Waigel for talks about revaluing central bank currency reserves, a spokesman from the German Finance Ministry said.
"Tietmeyer has arrived for talks with Waigel," the spokesman told Reuters.

The government and the central bank are thought to be near a compromise in which the Bundesbank would agree to a revised revaluation plan that would allow it to transfer a portion of the profits to Bonn, but not in 1997.
Tietmeyer also said on Wednesday that he expected to reach a final agreement "very soon" when he meets Waigel this week.

Sources close to the Bundesbank have indicated the central bank might be willing to revalue its dollar reserves to between 1.50-1.55 marks, up from current book rate of 1.36 marks, but still well below the current market exchange rate.

The sources also said there was no longer any discussion of revaluing the central bank's gold reserves before the start of monetary union in 1999. The meeting on Thursday aims to end a bitter row between the fiercely independent central bank and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's beleaguered coalition over tapping Bundesbank reserves in its bid to qualify for Europe's single currency.
